facts.why: The year on the form is the release year. The camp is in wartime Germany, with the Fourth of July in camp and the escape after it; the real Stalag Luft III escape was March 1944. The film pages I read give no year, so the exact story year is unsure, but 1963 is not it.
facts.full: Eat fast, keep your head down. Prices subject to change. Form CF-76. 1963.

notes: Lines match: 250 men, Tom, Dick and Harry, Ashley-Pitt's dirt, Blythe's papers, Cavendish's choir, potato moonshine on the Fourth of July, 20 feet short, 76 out, the Swiss fence and the ball in the cooler (Wikipedia); 'Seventeen escape attempts.' 'Eighteen, sir.', 'It's shattering!' and Hilts's Berlin line verbatim (Wikiquote). Print problems, not fact errors: three printed dish lines are stubs with no food at all ('Hilts rides hard for the Swiss border.', 'Hilts throws his ball.', 'Ashley-Pitt hides the tunnel dirt.'). The house eggs line (rotten eggs in one basket) is in the data but not printed.

vibe.verdict: The camp canteen with Tom, Dick and Harry, Hilts's tag and the motorbike still feels right, but half the dish lines print with no food.
